the SRAM based accelerator is more suitable for the partitioning of a weight matrix with a large size.
the SRAM accelerator has a better performance in terms of latency and dynamic power, but the area and leakage power are much higher than the RRAM accelerator.
the RRAM based accelerator is more energy efficient and has a lower latency for a larger weight matrix size, but the SRAM based accelerator is better for a smaller matrix size.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SRAM accelerator is more suitable to be used for the large weight matrix, while the RRAM accelerator is better for the small weight matrix.
the RRAM accelerator can achieve the best energy-delay product (EDP) with a small number of partitions.
the RRAM accelerator has a better energy efficiency than the SRAM accelerator for the large weight matrix, while the SRAM accelerator has a better area efficiency.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the partitioning of the synaptic array into the SRAM/RRAM accelerators should be done carefully, taking into account the latency, energy, area, and leakage power.
a fine-grained partitioning may not always be the best choice in terms of energy efficiency, and the optimal partition size depends on the array architecture and the application.
